Work will be performed across multiple sites—Omitron's Beltsville, MD office plus Goddard (Greenbelt, MD), Johnson Space Center (Houston, TX), NSWC Dahlgren (VA), and Peterson SFB (CO). The announcement was published by Rob Garner at Goddard on September 29, 2026. The article is a standard news release with no quotes from NASA officials and no details on individual work order distribution or period start date.

title: NASA Adds New Science Investigations for Moon Base
article_summary: NASA announced on September 30, 2026 the selection of three new scientific payloads under the PRISM (Payloads for Lunar Surface Operations) program, to be delivered via Commercial Lunar Payload Services (CLPS) as part of the Moon Base initiative. The three instruments are: (1) LEMS-SP — a Lunar Environment Monitoring Station at the South Pole for tracking local conditions; (2) GIMLI — a Geophysical Investigation for Mapping Lunar Interior targeting underground lava tubes near Marius Hills; and (3) DISCO — a Depth Imager with Spectral and Color Optics for locating subsurface ice and analyzing ground stability. The stated goal is to gather survival-critical data on radiation, hazards, and resources before crewed missions, supporting both Artemis and eventual Mars operations.

title: Introducing Falcon ASR
article_summary: Falcon ASR is a 1.6B-parameter open-weight automatic speech recognition model from TII (UAE), built on top of the Falcon3-Audio foundation. Key technical findings: (1) It achieves 20.92% average WER across six Arabic test sets, beating the prior best published result of 23.17% — a meaningful ~2.25 percentage-point improvement on a challenging low-resource language family. (2) On internal Emirati dialect evaluation it scored 22.73% WER and 10.19% CER, outperforming Qwen3-Omni by 4.07pp — notable given Qwen3-Omni is a much larger multimodal model. (3) English performance is strong at 5.74% mean WER on test sets. (4) The model uses a single-stage training approach with no language flag — the same weights handle Arabic (MSA, Gulf, Emirati dialects), English, French, Spanish, and Portuguese.
